title: Old Wax or Oil Finish on Hardwood Floors: How It Gets Removed Before Refinishing
meta: Old wax or oil on hardwood floors must be sanded fully off before a new finish will stick. Wills Flooring explains the tests, the process and the Everett price.
keywords: remove wax from hardwood floors before refinishing, old oil finish hardwood floor refinish, can you refinish waxed hardwood floors, paste wax floor sanding, hardwood floor refinishing Everett WA, fisheye in floor finish

blocks.lead: A waxed or oiled hardwood floor has to be sanded all the way to bare wood before any modern finish will bond, which means a full sand and refinish at $3.99 per sq ft, never a $1.99 recoat.
blocks.detail: Wax and penetrating oil soak into the wood instead of sitting on top, so there is no film to screen. The good news is that a full sanding removes them completely when it is done right, and the floor underneath is usually excellent old-growth wood.

blocks.html: Everett's Riverside and Bayside neighborhoods are full of 1900s to 1920s houses whose fir and oak floors were maintained with paste wax for fifty years before anyone had heard of polyurethane. Others got a penetrating oil in the 1970s. Both feel great underfoot and both cause the same problem when a homeowner asks for a fresh coat: the new finish beads up, crawls into little craters and peels within weeks. Here is how we identify an old wax or oil finish, how it comes off, and what it changes about the quote.

blocks.text: How to tell what is on your Everett floor

head: Test
What you see
What it means
rows: Some finish or wax is present. Not conclusive on its own.
Soaks in and darkens the wood
Bare wood or a worn penetrating oil. Sanding is the only option.
Mineral spirits on a white rag, rubbed in a closet corner
Rag turns yellow or brown and the spot goes dull
Wax. Mineral spirits dissolve paste wax and nothing else.
Fingernail scratch in a low-traffic spot
Soft, smeary, leaves a mark you can buff out
Wax or oil. A film finish (poly or Swedish) would flake or resist.
Look at the sheen from a low angle
Soft glow, no plastic-looking surface, dark buildup near walls
Wax buildup. Edges are where it collects because nobody walks there.
blocks.note: We run these tests at the free estimate. In Everett houses built before 1930 we assume wax until proven otherwise.

blocks.text: Why wax and a new finish do not mix

items.title: Fisheyes and crawling
items.text: Wax is a release agent. Even a trace left in the grain makes water-based finish pull back into round craters called fisheyes. You cannot fix them by adding another coat; the second coat crawls too.

items.title: No adhesion
items.text: Polyurethane needs to grip a scratched, clean surface. Over wax or oil it dries as a loose skin. It looks fine for a month, then peels at the doorway where feet twist.

items.title: Screening cannot remove it
items.text: A screen and recoat abrades a film finish so the new coat can bond. Wax has no film, and screening just smears warm wax deeper into the pores and gums up the screen. That is why the $1.99 option is off the table.

items.title: It loads the sandpaper
items.text: Wax melts under a drum sander and clogs the abrasive within a few feet. The crew changes paper far more often on the first cut, which is the extra time you may see on a wax job.

blocks.note: Choose natural or stain, not recoat, if your floor is waxed or oiled. Any extra sanding passes for heavy wax buildup are identified at the free estimate before you sign.

items.text: We test a corner with mineral spirits, check board thickness and look for wax buildup along baseboards and under radiators. You get a firm written price, either natural or stained.
items.note: Example: a 700 sq ft Riverside bungalow, natural finish with dust containment: 700 × $3.99 + $250 = $3,043

items.d: Day 1 morning · strip the heavy spots
items.text: Where wax has built up thick, along walls and in the dining room, we hand-strip with solvent and a scraper first. This keeps the sanders from smearing a quarter inch of wax across the whole room.

The first pass uses aggressive grit to take the surface down past anything the oil or wax soaked into, usually a thirty-second of an inch. Paper is swapped constantly. Edges and corners get the same cut with the edger and scraper.

items.d: Day 2 · medium and fine cuts, then a test patch
items.text: After the finer grits, we wipe a test area with finish and let it flash. If it lays flat with no craters, the floor is clean. If not, that area gets another pass before any coating goes on the whole floor.
Three coats of Bona water-based finish, or stain plus finish if you chose a color. From here the job is identical to any other sand and refinish.

blocks.text: Wax and penetrating oil are not the same problem

a.title: What to expect
items: Sits mostly in the top layer and in the pores
Dissolves in mineral spirits, so heavy spots can be pre-stripped
Clogs sandpaper fast; the coarse cut is slower
Once sanded off it is gone; no lingering odor
Can be stained afterward without trouble

b.title: What to expect
items: Soaks deeper into softer species like fir
Does not dissolve easily; only sanding removes it
Old oil can darken the wood unevenly, so stain may look patchy
Test patch is mandatory before finish
Some owners choose to keep it and re-oil instead

blocks.title: About that re-oil option:
blocks.text: If your Everett floor has a hardwax oil finish in good shape and you like the look, re-oiling the worn areas is a legitimate maintenance path and does not need a full sand. It is a different product and a different service from refinishing, so ask us which one your floor actually has before you choose.
When you should not strip a waxed floor

items.html: The wood is too thin. Century-old fir in Bayside has often been sanded before. If less than about 3/32 of an inch remains above the tongue, the coarse cut needed to remove oil can expose nails. We measure at a register or a threshold before quoting.

You are selling as-is. A clean, freshly waxed original floor reads as charming to many buyers of Everett's older homes. Spending on a full refinish only pays back when the floor is visibly worn or stained.
You love the low-sheen look. Matte water-based finish gets close, but wax has a depth nothing else copies. If that is why you bought the house, keep waxing it.
The floor is soft underfoot. Wax does not cause bounce or soft spots, and neither will refinishing fix them. That is a joist or subfloor conversation first.

blocks.text: What to ask any contractor before they sand a waxed floor

items.html: Did you test for wax? If they did not rub a corner with solvent, they are guessing. A crew surprised by wax on day one is a crew that will rush.
Is the quote for a full sand or a recoat? A recoat quote on a waxed floor is either a mistake or a job that will fail. Read our refinish or recoat post for the line between the two.
Will you do a finish test patch? This is the only proof the wax is gone. It takes twenty minutes and saves a whole floor.

What about the fumes from stripping? Solvent stripping of heavy spots is short and small in scale. We ventilate and, with dust containment, run the air scrubber. Everett's damp winters mean windows stay closed, so ask how they handle it.

Who stands behind it? Wills Flooring is Bona Certified and covers every refinish with a 1-year workmanship warranty, adhesion included. A peeling finish over missed wax is exactly what a warranty is for.

faq.q: Can you just put polyurethane over a waxed floor?
faq.a: No. The finish will crater, fail to bond and peel within weeks. Every trace of wax has to be sanded out of the wood first. Chemical wax removers alone are not enough for a whole floor; they help on heavy spots before sanding.

faq.q: Does removing wax cost more than a normal refinish?
faq.a: Wills Flooring's sand and refinish rate is $3.99 per sq ft natural or $6.50 with stain, the same as any floor. Heavy buildup can add sanding time, and if that applies to your floor we say so at the free estimate rather than adding it later.

faq.q: How do I know if my Everett floor is waxed or oiled?
faq.a: Rub a hidden spot with mineral spirits on a white rag. Yellow or brown residue and a dulled spot means wax. If nothing transfers but water still soaks in and darkens the wood, it is likely an old penetrating oil. Either way it needs full sanding.

faq.q: Can a waxed floor be stained a new color after sanding?
faq.a: Yes, once it is sanded to clean bare wood. Old penetrating oil is the exception: it can leave darker patches in softer boards, so we test the stain on the actual floor first and tell you if the result will be uneven.

faq.q: Will the wax smell linger after refinishing?
faq.a: No. Wax comes off with the sawdust. Any solvent used on heavy spots flashes off within hours, well before the first coat of finish goes down.

faq.q: Can I keep waxing my floor instead of refinishing it?
faq.a: You can, as long as the wood is not worn through or badly stained. Strip and re-wax every few years and buff in between. Just know that the day you want a durable modern finish, the whole floor gets sanded regardless.
